checks.result: The changed seam replaces sandboxes.connected(...) with connected_resources(...), retaining the select against next_nudge and the resource binding across serve. Base and extracted Tensorlake hooks both enter the credential lease before awaiting delivery, then retain it while awaiting tunnels. A winning nudge drops the hook future before the loop can acknowledge parked. This is preservation of the assigned extraction, not a new cancellation mechanism.

The required hook contract says: 'Cancellation must drop partially acquired leases. Their lifetime covers the hook-to-Connected publication gap and ends before a hold parks.' Both concrete hooks enter before delivery.connect.await and keep the lease through tunnel acquisition. Podman's credential field is initialized before its tunnel-field await; the partially constructed aggregate retains ownership and is dropped on cancellation. ConnectedResources owns both optional leases.

The recipe read is awaited before any view registration or worker spawn. The post-read registration/spawn-to-TunnelLease-return region contains no await (the awaits inside the spawned worker do not suspend acquisition). Cancellation while reading has no worker to strand; after spawn the owning lease is returned in the same acquisition poll. Drop aborts the worker, calls client.retire(), removes the host view, and bumps events. At 04ff the relevant no-await region is 109-168, not the later 137-182 numbering.

Drop synchronously decrements a reusable watch count; enter can raise zero to one and clears binding on that transition. push selects the current zero predicate with biased ordering, including while waiting on the serial lock. This proves release of hook registration, not a latched cancellation event: an unpolled push can still miss 1 -> 0 -> 1. The latest record's 288-299 and 375-406 references fit 566/tip; 04ff enter is 257-270. No blanket before-next-poll guarantee is inferred from the docstring or select.
